docs.title: Ally X Lean Win11
docs.text:
Short field guide for a lean Windows 11 USB install on ASUS ROG Ally X (RC72LA) without relying on ASUS Cloud Recovery: official ISO, CodingWonders/MicroWin, offline DISM driver injection, then G-Helper on the device.

Use the tabs and sidebar to move through steps in order. Each page is intentionally small.

docs.title: Machine that builds the image (PC)
docs.text:
• Windows 10/11 x64 with enough free disk space (tens of GB for ISO + extracted tree + mount scratch).
  • Administrator PowerShell or elevated session for Mount-WindowsImage / DISM.
  • Tools:
  • File archiver (for example NanaZip / 7-Zip) to extract ISO contents or mount ISO in Explorer.
  • Rufus (recommended) for the first bootable USB from the MicroWin ISO. Avoid stacking Rufus Windows User Experience tweaks on top of an already customized MicroWin ISO.
  • Folders (create if missing):
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "C:\WinWork\Mount"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "C:\DRIVERS"

docs.title: USB flash drive (install media)
docs.text:
• This manual uses E:\ for the USB on the PC that prepares the stick. On the Ally, the boot menu label is firmware-defined (not necessarily E:).
  • install.wim is often larger than 4 GiB. A single FAT32-only volume cannot store it. Typical Rufus Windows 11 layouts use NTFS (or a supported split layout).

docs.title: Physical connection on ROG Ally X (USB-C)
docs.text:
The handheld top port is USB-C. A normal USB-A installer stick will not plug in directly. Use one of:

Approach Notes USB-C to USB-A adapter plus standard USB pendrive Use a data adapter (not charge-only). USB-C flash drive Simplest cable-wise. Dock / hub with downstream USB-A UEFI must list the stick as a boot device - behavior varies by dock firmware.

Example: validation used a Dell Universal Dock UD22 (USB-C from the Ally to the dock, USB-A installer in the dock). Other USB-C docks may work; if the BIOS does not show the USB installer, try a direct C-to-A adapter or native C flash drive first.

docs.title: Windows edition (Home vs Pro)
docs.text: ROG Ally X is often sold with Windows 11 Home. You may install Pro (or Home) according to your license. Edition does not remove the need for the same chipset + WLAN packages on custom media.

docs.title: BIOS and boot menu (volume down)
docs.text:
1. Power off fully (not sleep).
  2. Press Power to turn on.
  3. Immediately press Volume down repeatedly until BIOS or Boot menu appears.
  4. ASUS FAQ: ROG Ally series FAQ (UK).
  5. Community: Reddit - access BIOS.
  6. Broader context: Asus-ROG-Ally-Guide - Getting Started.

From Windows: Settings → System → Recovery → Advanced startup → UEFI Firmware Settings.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
• Update BIOS from ASUS when convenient.
  • Keep a second copy of a working install.wim / USB; custom images are your responsibility.

docs.title: Step 1 - Download official Windows 11 (x64 ISO)
docs.text:
Use Microsoft’s software download page:

  • Download Windows 11 (Microsoft, en-US)

Create the ISO through the site’s flow (disk image section for x64 devices).

docs.title: Confirm the file (example paths)
docs.text: Get-Item "C:\Users\YourName\Downloads\Win11_x64.iso" | Format-List Name, Length, LastWriteTime

docs.title: Optional: mount the ISO
docs.text:
Mount-DiskImage -ImagePath "C:\Users\YourName\Downloads\Win11_x64.iso"
Get-Volume | Where-Object FileSystemLabel -match "CCCOMA" | Format-List DriveLetter, FileSystemLabel

Note the drive letter (for example F:). MicroWin will need F:\sources\install.wim (and the rest of that layout).

Unmount when finished:

Dismount-DiskImage -ImagePath "C:\Users\YourName\Downloads\Win11_x64.iso"

docs.title: Step 2 - Build MicroWin image (CodingWonders)
docs.text:
MicroWin was removed from Chris Titus WinUtil; the maintained continuation is the .NET project CodingWonders/MicroWin. Read the README, roadmap, and Releases.

The upstream README states the app is beta, not code-signed, and must run as Administrator (you may need an antivirus exclusion).

docs.title: Option A - Install from latest release
docs.text:
1. Open Releases on GitHub.
  2. Download the latest Windows x64 build archive.
  3. Extract to a folder, for example C:\Tools\MicroWin\.
  4. Run the application as Administrator and follow the UI to select your official Windows 11 ISO (or sources\install.wim, per tool guidance), edition, and debloat options.
  5. If the tool can import a driver folder, point it at C:\DRIVERS after you removed problematic packages (see 03-drivers-asus.md).
  6. Export a MicroWin ISO, for example microwin-win11-pro.iso.

docs.title: Option B - One-liner (from upstream README)
docs.text:
Review upstream security notes before running:

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CodingWonders/MicroWin/refs/heads/main/Microwin.ps1 | iex"

docs.title: Create bootable USB (first time)
docs.text:
Use Rufus:

  1. Select the MicroWin ISO and the USB device.
  2. If Rufus offers Windows User Experience / extra image tweaks, disable them when the ISO is already customized by MicroWin (double-patching causes failures; background in winutil#3936).

You should see on the USB (example letter E:\):

  • E:\sources\install.wim
  • E:\sources\boot.wim
  • E:\boot, E:\EFI, E:\setup.exe, …

docs.title: Folder layout instead of mounting
docs.text:
<extracted>\sources\install.wim
<extracted>\sources\boot.wim

Example size check:

Get-Item "C:\path\to\microwin-win11-pro\sources\install.wim" | Format-List FullName, Length

docs.title: Step 3 - ASUS drivers for ROG Ally X (RC72LA)
Why inject anything
docs.text: ASUS Cloud Recovery ships an image that already matches the handheld. A retail or MicroWin USB can fail early with Windows Setup could not install one or more boot-critical drivers if WinPE / Setup does not load the right stack before the OS is applied. Offline injection into install.wim (and sources\boot.wim when needed) fixes that. Details: 04-dism-offline-drivers.md.

docs.title: Where C:\DRIVERS comes from
docs.text:
Download ZIP packages from ASUS support for ROG Ally X RC72LA (pick your region; product selector must match Ally X, not the older Ally SKU):

  • ROG Ally - Helpdesk (download hub, US)

Extract each ZIP, then run the vendor Setup.exe (or equivalent). In the wizard choose Extract, not Install. The tool will create a subfolder under C:\DRIVERS automatically, for example:

C:\DRIVERS\DolbyAtmosdriverforROG_TUF_ASUS_Z_V3.30704.742

Point DISM at the parent C:\DRIVERS (or a cleaned copy) so all extracted .inf trees are visible.

docs.title: Minimal set for the image (DISM)
docs.text:
Keep the offline folder small and safe:

Priority Package (typical name on ASUS site) Notes Required AMD Chipset (DriverOnly tree) Strip PMF and MSI noise first (below). Required MediaTek WLAN (often includes BT) Wi-Fi for Setup and first boot.

Everything else (AMD graphics, audio, Realtek USB LAN, motion, card reader, controller INFs, BIOS-facing tools) can usually wait for G-Helper and Windows Update after install, unless you already know you need them in PE.

docs.title: Fingerprint (do not blind-inject)
docs.text:
RC72LA can ship FocalTech or EgisTec sensors. The wrong INF tree stages but does not bind (no Biometric class device). Do not guess both vendors into the WIM unless you accept bloat and cleanup later.

  • Prefer: install the correct FOCAL or EGIS package after Windows is up, from the same ASUS page, then remove orphans with RAPR if needed. See troubleshooting-fingerprint.md.

docs.title: Skip or delete before Add-WindowsDriver
docs.text:
Item Reason PMF_7040Series / amdpmf.inf Known Add-WindowsDriver failure on some MicroWin images; handheld can run without PMF in the WIM. ROGScreenManager, Package, Install.bat Apps / launchers, not bare class drivers. Dolby Atmos driver bundle (optional) Often fine, but if it causes store clutter or bad pairs, install later or remove with RAPR.

Example removal (adjust folder names to match your extract):

Remove-Item -LiteralPath "C:\DRIVERS\<ChipsetFolder>\PMF_7040Series Driver" -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

docs.title: Driver store cleanup
docs.text:
Driver Store Explorer (RAPR) removes stuck packages (wrong fingerprint vendor, Dolby, duplicates). Install and launch:

winget install lostindark.DriverStoreExplorer --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements
rapr

Full workflow: troubleshooting-driver-store-rapr.md.

docs.title: Step 4 - Offline driver injection into install.wim (DISM / PowerShell)
docs.text:
Without injection (or Cloud Recovery), a generic Windows 11 USB often fails at the beginning with boot-critical drivers on Ally X class hardware. Servicing install.wim fixes the installed OS copy; servicing boot.wim (section 4.6) fixes early Setup / WinPE when the error appears before disk selection.

Replace paths with yours:

  • Source WIM: C:\path\to\microwin-win11-pro\sources\install.wim
  • Mount point: C:\WinWork\Mount
  • Drivers: C:\DRIVERS (cleaned per 03-drivers-asus.md)

Run PowerShell as Administrator.

docs.title: 4.1 List editions / indexes
docs.text:
Get-WindowsImage -ImagePath "C:\path\to\microwin-win11-pro\sources\install.wim"

Pick the Index that matches your edition (Pro, Home, …).

docs.title: 4.2 Mount the image
docs.text:
There must be a space between -ImagePath and the quoted path.

Wrong:

Mount-WindowsImage -Path C:\WinWork\Mount\ -ImagePath"C:\...\install.wim" -Index 1

Correct:

Mount-WindowsImage -Path "C:\WinWork\Mount" `
  -ImagePath "C:\path\to\microwin-win11-pro\sources\install.wim" `
  -Index 1

docs.title: 4.3 Add drivers (recursive)
docs.text:
Add-WindowsDriver -Path "C:\WinWork\Mount" -Driver "C:\DRIVERS" -Recurse -Verbose
  • First run may stop on the first fatal package; -Verbose shows which .inf failed.
  • If amdpmf.inf (PMF) fails, remove that folder from C:\DRIVERS and run Add-WindowsDriver again. Already-staged drivers usually remain.

docs.title: 4.4 Verify (optional)
docs.text: Get-WindowsDriver -Path "C:\WinWork\Mount" | Format-Table -AutoSize ClassName, BootCritical, ProviderName, Version, OriginalFileName

docs.title: 4.5 Commit and unmount
docs.text:
Dismount-WindowsImage -Path "C:\WinWork\Mount" -Save

Logs: C:\Windows\Logs\DISM\dism.log and, before dismount, C:\WinWork\Mount\Windows\INF\setupapi.dev.log.

docs.title: 4.6 (Optional) Same drivers into boot.wim
docs.text:
If Setup still fails in WinPE, repeat mount → Add-WindowsDriver → Dismount -Save for each index of ...\sources\boot.wim:

Get-WindowsImage -ImagePath "C:\path\to\microwin-win11-pro\sources\boot.wim"

Mount index 1, add a smaller driver set (chipset + MediaTek + storage if needed), save; repeat for index 2 (names vary - trust Get-WindowsImage).

docs.title: Step 5 - Put the modified install.wim on the USB (E:\)
docs.text:
You do not need to rebuild a full ISO or re-run Rufus only to swap the OS image file, as long as the stick is already a valid Windows Setup layout.

On ROG Ally X: there is no built-in USB-A port. Use a USB-C installer, USB-C to USB-A adapter plus a stick, or a USB-C dock that exposes a bootable mass-storage device (see 00-prerequisites.md - Physical connection).

docs.title: 5.1 Confirm USB layout
docs.text:
Get-ChildItem "E:\" | Format-Wide -Column 4
Test-Path "E:\sources\install.wim"
Get-Item "E:\sources\install.wim" | Format-List FullName, Length, LastWriteTime

docs.title: 5.2 Backup the old WIM (recommended)
docs.text: Rename-Item -Path "E:\sources\install.wim" -NewName "install.wim.bak_$(Get-Date -Format yyyyMMdd_HHmm)"

docs.title: 5.3 Copy the serviced WIM
docs.text:
Source must be the same file you mounted in 04-dism-offline-drivers.md and dismounted with -Save.

Copy-Item -LiteralPath "C:\path\to\microwin-win11-pro\sources\install.wim" `
  -Destination "E:\sources\install.wim" -Force

Get-Item "E:\sources\install.wim" | Format-List FullName, Length, LastWriteTime

docs.title: 5.4 Filesystem constraints
docs.text:
• If install.wim > 4 GiB, FAT32 cannot hold it. Use a Rufus layout that supports large WIMs (often NTFS on the data partition).
  • If the USB uses install.esd, do not rename .wim to .esd - the media type must match what setup.exe expects.

docs.title: 5.5 Boot the Ally X from USB
docs.text: Power off, use Volume Down + Power (or your firmware’s documented combo) to open the Boot menu, then select the USB entry.

docs.title: 5.6 If you also modified boot.wim
docs.text:
Copy-Item -LiteralPath "C:\path\to\microwin-win11-pro\sources\boot.wim" `
  -Destination "E:\sources\boot.wim" -Force

docs.title: Step 6 - After Windows is on the Ally X (RC72LA)
6.1 G-Helper
docs.text: Use G-Helper for performance modes, GPU modes, fan curves, charge cap, display refresh, LEDs where supported, and driver / BIOS links for your model. Install ASUS System Control Interface v3 from ASUS if G-Helper reports it missing.

docs.title: 6.2 Apps and tweaks (winget or WinUtil only)
docs.text:
• Individual packages: prefer winget install … for well-known IDs.
  • Bulk tweaker / installer profile: use WinUtil with a JSON config. See winget-profile.md for this repo’s exported list and drift warning.

Automation docs: WinUtil - Automation.

Dry run (no apply):

& ([ScriptBlock]::Create((irm "https://christitus.com/win"))) -Config "C:\path\to\your-config.json"

Apply:

& ([ScriptBlock]::Create((irm "https://christitus.com/win"))) -Config "C:\path\to\your-config.json" -Run

Keep personal configs private if they encode aggressive removals.

docs.title: 6.3 Optional: OpenSSH Server
docs.text: Not required for this guide. If you want remote PowerShell over SSH, enable OpenSSH Server (and firewall rules) through WinUtil optional features / tweaks rather than ad-hoc downloads. See WinUtil’s UI and documentation for the current toggle names.

docs.title: 6.4 Name and address on the LAN
docs.text:
Windows may show a default computer name until you change it under Settings → System → About.

To see this device’s IPv4 on the network (for example from another PC on the same Wi-Fi), on the handheld open Windows Terminal and run:

ipconfig

Use the Wireless LAN adapter Wi-Fi IPv4 address. DHCP can change it after a lease renew.

docs.title: 6.5 Maintenance
docs.text:
1. BIOS / MCU / PD firmware from ASUS when release notes matter.
  2. G-Helper → Updates for driver deltas.
  3. Windows Update for security and runtime payloads deferred by MicroWin.

docs.title: Driver Store Explorer (RAPR) - clean old / wrong / Dolby packages
docs.text:
Use Driver Store Explorer (RAPR) when pnputil or Settings → Apps does not remove a driver package cleanly - for example unused FOCAL after switching to EGIS, or Dolby Atmos packages that resist normal uninstall.

Read the upstream README once: the tool modifies the Windows driver store; wrong deletions can break boot. Prefer deleting packages you recognize and create a restore point first: lostindark/DriverStoreExplorer.

docs.title: Install (winget)
docs.text:
winget install lostindark.DriverStoreExplorer --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements

Launch:

rapr

Or start Driver Store Explorer from the Start menu. Run as Administrator.

docs.title: Basic workflow
docs.text:
1. Create a restore point (recommended): Settings → System → About → System protection → Create for C:.
  2. Open Driver Store Explorer elevated; wait for the list to load.
  3. Search examples:
  4. Focal / FtWbio / ftwbio - wrong fingerprint vendor on an Egis unit.
  5. Dolby / DAX3 / dax3 - Dolby / APO extension packages.
  6. Select rows; verify Provider, Driver Class, Version, Device name.
  7. Delete Driver(s).

If deletion fails, use force (next section).

docs.title: Force delete (Dolby and similar)
docs.text:
1. Search Dolby, DAX3, or the .inf name from Device Manager → Driver → Driver Details.
  2. Select the row.
  3. Delete Driver(s); enable Force Deletion / Force remove if the UI offers it (wording varies by RAPR version).
  4. If several Dolby rows exist, remove obsolete versions first; keep what your current Realtek stack still needs if you use Dolby.

After force removal: reboot. Reinstall from ASUS or Microsoft Store only if you still need Atmos.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Old drivers: RAPR can select old driver(s) when multiple versions exist - review before delete.
  • Gray device names: disconnected hardware; safe to remove if you will reinstall when reconnecting.
  • Export in RAPR backs up selected packages before aggressive cleanup.

docs.title: Command-line alternative
docs.text:
pnputil /enum-drivers | findstr /i dolby dax3 focal ftwbio
# pnputil /delete-driver oemNNN.inf /uninstall /force

docs.title: Related docs
docs.text:
• troubleshooting-fingerprint.md - Focal vs Egis; wrong stack removal.
  • 03-drivers-asus.md - what to inject vs install live.

docs.title: Fingerprint: "We couldn't find a fingerprint scanner" (ROG Ally X RC72LA)
Root cause (hardware variants)
docs.text:
ROG Ally X RC72LA units ship with one of two fingerprint USB stacks:

Vendor Typical USB ID ASUS driver package FocalTech USB\VID_2808&PID_A753 FOCAL Fingerprint (FtWbio UMDF) EgisTec USB\VID_1C7A&PID_0588 EGIS Fingerprint

The FOCAL INF (FtWbioDriverUmdf.inf) only matches USB\VID_2808&PID_A753. On Egis (1C7A:0588), FOCAL may stage but nothing binds - PnP has no Biometric class device - Windows Hello shows no scanner.

This is not fixed by generic "debloat" alone when HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Biometrics is absent.

docs.title: Verify on the handheld (PowerShell)
docs.text:
Get-PnpDevice | Where-Object { $_.InstanceId -match 'VID_2808&PID_A753' }

Get-PnpDevice | Where-Object { $_.InstanceId -match 'VID_1C7A&PID_0588' } |
  Format-List Status, Class, FriendlyName, InstanceId

If you see USB\VID_1C7A&PID_0588 as a USB device before EGIS install, use the EGIS package from ASUS for RC72LA, not Focal.

pnputil /enum-devices /class Biometric
# "No devices were found" = no bound WBF biometric driver yet

docs.title: Fix (manual)
docs.text:
1. ASUS support - ROG Ally X (2024) RC72LA - Driver & Tools - Windows 11 64-bit.
  2. Download EGIS Fingerprint Driver (or FOCAL if your hardware ID matches Focal).
  3. Run the vendor installer or Device Manager → Update driver pointed at the extracted INF folder.
  4. Reboot.
  5. Optional: set Windows Biometric Service to automatic:
Set-Service WbioSrvc -StartupType Automatic
Start-Service WbioSrvc
  1. Settings → Accounts → Sign-in options → Fingerprint recognition.

docs.title: If you already installed the wrong package
docs.text:
• Install the correct vendor package, then run Windows Update optional drivers once.
  • Remove unused packages from the driver store with RAPR - troubleshooting-driver-store-rapr.md (winget install lostindark.DriverStoreExplorer, search Focal / FtWbio, delete or force delete if needed).

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Focal vs Egis split (Linux-oriented thread, still useful IDs): bazzite issue #3752.
  • G-Helper links to official ASUS driver pages per model: seerge/g-helper.

docs.title: WinUtil package list (winget.json)
docs.text: The repository root file winget.json (next to README.md when you clone or download this repo) is an exported WinUtil automation profile: an array of WPFInstall… / WPFTweaks… / WPFFeatures… toggle IDs.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
Follow WinUtil automation: pass that JSON as -Config (dry run without -Run, apply with -Run after you review).

Example (adjust the path to where you cloned or copied the file):

& ([ScriptBlock]::Create((irm "https://christitus.com/win"))) -Config "C:\path\to\rog-allyx-rc72la-win11-manual\winget.json" -Run

docs.title: IDs drift after updates
docs.text: WinUtil renames or drops toggles between releases. After a WinUtil or winget ecosystem update, open WinUtil, re-export your profile, and diff against this file. Treat the committed list as a starting template, not a guaranteed-stable contract.
